preconditions.expression: len(s1) == len(s2) and all(c in {'x', 'y'} for c in s1) and all(c in {'x', 'y'} for c in s2)
preconditions.description: Both strings s1 and s2 have equal length and contain only characters 'x' or 'y'.

postconditions.expression: return_value == -1 or (return_value >= 0 and all(s1[i] == s2[i] for i in range(len(s1))))
postconditions.description: If return_value is -1, it means it is impossible to make s1 and s2 equal. Otherwise, return_value is the minimum number of swaps required to make s1 and s2 equal, and the strings are equal after performing those swaps.

postconditions.expression: return_value == -1 if sum(s1.count('x') - s2.count('x')) != 0 else return_value >= 0
postconditions.description: If the total number of 'x's in s1 and s2 differ, return -1. Otherwise, return_value is the minimum number of swaps required.

postconditions.expression: all(s1[i] == s2[i] for i in range(len(s1))) or return_value == -1
postconditions.description: The function returns -1 if and only if it is impossible to make s1 and s2 equal; otherwise, the returned swaps make them equal.
